sections.heading: Buildkite buyer question and thesis
sections.body:
log management; CI/CD and automation; developer AI assistance; enterprise security and SSO. Free · free · log management | Pro | Enterprise. Github, Slack. Teams that want specialist CI/CD with self-hosted agents against an existing git remote; Buyers comparing Buildkite Pro list price to CircleCI Performance list price and GitHub Actions minutes; Orgs that will not move source control in order to buy CI. Buildkite is a CI/CD platform (pipelines, self-hosted agents, hosted agents) — not a Git host. It lives in source-control-devops so DevOps buyers can compare it with CircleCI, GitH. That catalogue mix is the Buildkite implementation filter — not a generic it-development lecture.

Buyer question: does Pro gating log management change the Buildkite decision before seats scale?

Decision thesis: unlike a generic it-development shortlist, Buildkite is worth it if Teams that want specialist CI/CD with self-hosted agents against an existing git remote outweighs Not a git host — you still need GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket for source control — trade-off accepted before seats scale.

Best for: Teams that want specialist CI/CD with self-hosted agents against an existing git remote; Buyers comparing Buildkite Pro list price to CircleCI Performance list price and GitHub Actions minutes; Orgs that will not move source control in order to buy CI (Teams that want specialist CI/CD with self-hosted agents against an existing git remote).

Poor fit when: Teams whose primary purchase is a git host (GitHub / GitLab); Observability or on-call purchases; Hosting panel or managed WordPress hosting. Avoid if Not a git host — you still need GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket for source control would block go-live.

sections.heading: Buildkite limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Not a git host — you still need GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket for source control; Same source-control-devops cluster as GitHub, but GitHub the SCM is a different primary shape; Does not outrank GitHub (9.1) because it forces process changes or add-ons around Buildkite when log management is the job.

Pricing interpretation: stay on Free until log management is mandatory; plan jumps to Pro only after that hinge is proven.

Plan trade-off: you gain log management at the expense of Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Free · free · log management | Pro | Enterprise.

Alternative context: unlike CircleCI, Buildkite is preferable when Teams that want specialist CI/CD with self-hosted agents against an existing git remote because log management plus log management match; prefer CircleCI when Teams whose primary purchase is a git host (GitHub / GitLab) because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Buildkite
sections.body:
Scenario: for log management teams, recommend Buildkite when Teams that want specialist CI/CD with self-hosted agents against an existing git remote; recommend an alternative path when Teams whose primary purchase is a git host (GitHub / GitLab) because Not a git host — you still need GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket for source control dominates.

Implementation effort: setup takes a named admin for log management plus a freeze window if Github are in the cutover path.

Integrations in research: Github, Slack.

Final call: proceed with Buildkite when log management plus log management outweigh Not a git host — you still need GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket for source control; walk when Teams whose primary purchase is a git host (GitHub / GitLab) because workarounds will eat the Pro spend.
